Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for walking us through the demo earlier — the latency numbers look promising. A few immediate networking questions that came up on the call so we can scope Private VPC readiness: 

- We plan to keep worker subnets in our VPC and would like Redwood to connect via PrivateLink if possible. Is there a size limit or account quota we should know about?
- For egress, we prefer to route outbound traffic through our customer-managed NAT/Bastion (we want to preserve our egress IPs). Is that supported or does Redwood require outgoing connections from your side?

Thanks,

Hi Anna — great next steps, thank you for the diagram and ranges. Quick recap below and proposed owners/timeline so we can align before the security questionnaire: 

Summary answers (high level):
- PrivateLink support: Yes — Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink endpoint services for Private VPC. We'll need you to create an endpoint in your account and allow our service. No hard limit beyond standard AWS quotas; if you have >500 endpoints we can discuss alternatives.
- Customer-managed egress: Supported. We can host the connection such that outbound model calls originate from Redwood's subnet but we can route through your NAT/bastion using symmetric routing or have your NAT act as the egress for calls destined to third-party APIs. We will need an egress IP range to allow on our side for callbacks/text classifications (if applicable).
- TLS: For PrivateLink, TLS stays end-to-end by default; if you have a TLS inspection appliance, we recommend peering + in-VPC proxies. We can document the handshake and SNI expectations.

Immediate asks from our side (please provide by EOD Wed):
1) Confirm VPC ID, region, and the subnet IDs you plan to use for the interface endpoint.
2) Provide the NAT/bastion public IP(s) you want Redwood to expect as egress (or confirm you want Redwood egressing from our managed IPs).
3) Indicate whether you require split-horizon DNS (internal name -> private IP) or if a single endpoint hostname is fine.

Owners/timeline: 
- Tessa (sales): coordinate approval and security questionnaire (this week)
- Ben (infra eng): technical lead for Privatelink/peering feasibility (please advise on port list & certificate needs) — target: 2 business days
- Connor (network): will own IP allowlist and egress model options with your NetOps — target: 3 business days

I'll follow up with a short checklist for the security questionnaire items you mentioned. Looping Ben and Connor in here so they can pick up the technical details.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Thanks — quick post-demo network questions

Anna — thanks for the diagram, that helped. A few technical clarifications from our infra perspective (so we can pick the cleanest path):

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering tradeoffs:
   - PrivateLink (recommended): minimal routing changes in your VPC, supports endpoint service model, preserves your VPC isolation. Works well when you want simple ingress from your VPC to our service.
   - VPC Peering (use-case): if you require in-VPC TLS inspection appliances to inspect traffic or need low-level network visibility, peering (+ route table entries) is sometimes easier. Peering can complicate cross-account NAT egress unless you use our managed NAT.

2) Egress strategies we support:
   - Customer egress (preferred for your compliance): You NAT outbound model calls through your NAT/Bastion. We'll accept connections routed via PrivateLink interface endpoint; for third-party callbacks Redwood may need to reach out to your IPs — provide the public egress IP list.
   - Redwood-managed egress: Redwood egresses from our pool of IPs and we provide the list; useful if you can't NAT-traverse.

3) DNS & TLS notes:
   - If you need split-horizon DNS, we provide the canonical endpoint hostname (svc.redwood-inference.net). You can map it to the interface endpoint private IP internally.
   - For TLS inspection, peering with in-VPC proxies is simpler because PrivateLink terminates on our side and the TLS connection is end-to-end. If you require inspection, we'll document the SNI and TLS fingerprint to allow your appliance to decrypt and inspect.

Port list we need opened (TCP): 443 (HTTPS) outbound to our endpoint. If you plan to use metrics callbacks or Prometheus scraping, provide the port(s) separately.

Connor, can you coordinate a short runbook for the IP allowlist and the interface endpoint handshake? Anna, if you can confirm the subnet IDs and whether your NetOps prefers PrivateLink or peering, we'll produce a final plan.

–Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick responses inline and next steps from Sofia Ops: 

> Quick recap answers (high level): PrivateLink support: Yes 
We prefer PrivateLink. We'll create the interface endpoint in us-east-1. Subnets: private-subnet-a (subnet-0a1), private-subnet-b (subnet-0b2).

> Customer-managed egress: Supported.
We will provide NAT public IPs. List attached in the spreadsheet. For callbacks, we plan to allow Redwood-managed IPs to reach our webhook endpoint; can you send the list of Redwood egress IPs as well?

> TLS: For PrivateLink, TLS stays end-to-end by default; if you have TLS inspection appliance, we recommend peering...
We do have an in-line TLS inspector for a subset of traffic. We are fine with TLS end-to-end for model inference calls but require that any outbound third-party webhooks termination be configurable. If PrivateLink forces termination that blocks our inspector, we may opt for peering for those flows.

Action items (Sofia Ops):
- Rajiv: share the NAT public IPs and VPC/subnet IDs (attached).
- Ops: run quota check for interface endpoints and report back by EOD Monday.

Requests for Redwood: 
1) Please produce a short runbook for the PrivateLink interface acceptance handshake (what we need to accept service name, service ID, and which security group rules to apply).
2) Share Redwood egress IP list for callbacks/webhooks (or confirm if you need us to open inbound from svc.redwood-inference.net only).
3) Draft recommended config for split-horizon DNS if we choose PrivateLink but still want internal name resolution to our inspection appliance.

We'll upload a filled copy of your questionnaire later today. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Singh | Senior NetOps Engineer, Sofia Tech
